quote_item6: If the frequency value stated in the title was observed as the dominant spectral peak within a tolerance range of +/-3 Hz in the analysis, the content was considered technically verified.
quote_item10: A total of 150 different digital contents were selected using the criterion sampling technique, one of the purposive sampling methods. The main criteria were that the content had received at least 10,000 interactions and included a specific Hz value in its title or description section, such as 432 Hz, 528 Hz, or 639 Hz. ... The fact that the promised Hertz value was found in only 12 contents (8%) points to a serious inconsistency regarding the technical accuracy of content marketed as healing frequencies.
notes: Yuvaci, Journal for the Interdisciplinary Art and Education 2026. FFT spectrum analysis of 150 healing-frequency audio items drawn from seven platforms (YouTube 60, YouTube Music 20, Instagram 20, Fizy 15, Spotify 15, Apple Music 10, Deezer 10); no collection dates. Item1/2 HIGH: every item was selected because it already advertises a Hz value, so the universe is defined by the phenomenon being measured, and the seeds are the keywords 'frequency, meditation music, solfeggio frequencies, and healing sounds'. Item3 HIGH: explicit purposive criterion sampling, a 10,000-interaction popularity floor, and author-set platform quotas (40% YouTube). Items4-5 NA (content-only). Item6 LOW: falsity is decided instrumentally against the claim the item itself prints - the dominant spectral peak within +/-3 Hz of the titled value - which is an external, pre-existing standard rather than author-devised subjective coding, a quality rubric or guideline adherence. ANCHOR-JUDGEMENT TENSION, flagged not overridden: what is counted as false is a mislabelled Hz value, while the health claims attached to these frequencies (DNA repair, cellular resonance, liver detox) are described discursively but never adjudicated, so the case definition is externally anchored yet measures a narrower construct than the review's. Item7 LOW: a standard measurement instrument (digital spectrum analyser and Voxengo SPAN at 44.1 kHz, each file measured three times and averaged) plus a reported Krippendorff alpha of 0.82, which covers the discursive coding rather than the FFT, which needs no rater agreement. The dominant-peak rule is never validated against known-tuned audio, and a piece genuinely tuned to A = 432 Hz would fail it because its loudest partial is whatever note is playing, so the 92% is probably an overcount - recorded here because the anchor's failing condition (no reliability statistic AND no validated instrument) is not met. Item8 LOW: one FFT protocol applied identically to every audio file; the uneven platform mix is charged at items 2-3. Item9 HIGH: no collection dates, no observation window, all-time popular content generalised to prevalence. Item10 HIGH: the denominator is 150 items pre-selected for making a frequency claim and clearing 10,000 interactions - selected on the phenomenon and popularity-truncated - not any audience's diet.
